The '''43rd Academy Awards''' ceremony, presented by [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]], was held on April 15, 1971, and took place at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] to honor the best [[1970 in film|films of 1970]]. The Awards, without a host for the third consecutive year, were broadcast by [[NBC]] for the first time in 11 years.

[[George C. Scott]], winner of [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for ''[[Patton (film)|Patton]]'', became the first actor to decline an Oscar, having previously protested his nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for ''[[The Hustler]]'' ([[34th Academy Awards|1961]]) and quoted as saying that the Academy Awards were "a two-hour meat parade, a public display with contrived suspense for economic reasons".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/dvd/patton |title=Review of Patton |author=TotalFilm |access-date=2006-04-24 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110705124124/http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/dvd/patton |archive-date=July 5, 2011 }}</ref> He also maintained that it was "degrading for actors to compete against one another".<ref name="Oscars '70 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/844/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=845 |isbn=0-385-04060-1|author-link=David Wallechinsky|author-link2=Irving Wallace}}</ref> Co-star [[Karl Malden]] agreed, but felt that Scott could have made his denunciation more subtly.<ref name="Oscars '70 Notes"/>

With her [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] win for ''[[Airport (1970 film)|Airport]]'', [[Helen Hayes]] became the first performer to win Oscars in both lead and supporting categories (having won Best Actress [[5th Academy Awards|39 years before]] for ''[[The Sin of Madelon Claudet]]''). Her win set a record for the biggest gap between acting wins, subsequently broken by [[Katharine Hepburn]] (48 years between her [[6th Academy Awards|first]] and [[54th Academy Awards|last]] wins).

The documentary film ''[[Woodstock (film)|Woodstock]]'' garnered three Oscar nominations, making it the most nominated documentary film in Oscar history (its record was later tied by ''[[Flee (film)|Flee]]'', [[94th Academy Awards|51 years later]]).

This was the only time since the [[6th Academy Awards]] that all five nominees for Best Actress were first-time nominees, and was the last time that either lead acting category was entirely composed of new nominees until the [[95th Academy Awards]]. It was also the first time since the [[7th Academy Awards]] in which none of the nominees for the [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] had a previous nomination in that category.

As of 2024, this is the most recent ceremony in which the 4 highest-grossing films of the year were nominated for Best Picture (''Love Story'', ''Airport'', ''M*A*S*H'' and ''Patton'').

* To [[Orson Welles]] for superlative artistry and versatility in the creation of motion pictures.
